record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: What is the correct minimality theory for positive realizations of continuous-time systems? More specifically, for continuous-time positive systems, how should one characterize the minimal possible state dimension of a positive realization and what criteria determine whether a given positive realization is minimal?

evidence.quote: An obvious - but important - question is that of minimality of positive realizations for continuous-time systems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider continuous-time linear time-invariant systems of the form
  x'(t) = A x(t) + B u(t),  y(t) = C x(t) + D u(t),
where A ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, B ∈ ℝ^{n×m}, C ∈ ℝ^{p×n}, D ∈ ℝ^{p×m}. Such a quadruple (A, B, C, D) is called a positive realization if A is a Metzler matrix (i.e., its off-diagonal entries are nonnegative) and B, C, D have all entries nonnegative; equivalently, every nonnegative input u(·) and nonnegative initial state x(0) produces a nonnegative state trajectory x(·) and nonnegative output y(·). Given a proper rational transfer function H(s) (or, equivalently, an impulse response) that admits at least one positive realization, define the minimal positive realization dimension n⁺(H) to be the smallest integer n ≥ 0 for which there exists a positive realization (A, B, C, D) of H with state dimension n.

Problem: Develop a complete minimality theory for positive realizations of continuous-time systems. Specifically:
  (a) Provide a characterization of n⁺(H) in terms of the data of H (e.g., its Markov parameters, Hankel matrix factorizations over the nonnegative orthant, or geometric/cone-theoretic invariants), accounting for the fact that A must be Metzler rather than entrywise nonnegative as in the discrete-time case.
  (b) Provide necessary and sufficient conditions on a given positive realization (A, B, C, D) under which it is minimal, i.e., no positive realization of the same transfer function has strictly smaller state dimension.
artifact.status_search_result: The characterization of minimality for positive realizations, particularly in the continuous-time setting where the dynamics matrix must be Metzler rather than nonnegative, is widely acknowledged to remain an open problem. Recent surveys and research papers (including works from 2019–2024) continue to address only special cases (e.g., low-order systems, specific pole structures) and report partial bounds rather than a complete theory.

status_evidence.title: An upper bound on the dimension of minimal positive realizations for discrete time systems
status_evidence.snippet: Provides bounds rather than exact characterization, even in the discrete-time case.
status_evidence.claim: Only bounds are known, not a complete characterization.
